title: Platform events, change data capture, Pub/Sub API, and replay concepts

objectives: Distinguish custom platform events from Change Data Capture record-change events.
Describe Pub/Sub API as the gRPC interface to the event bus for publish/subscribe and schema.
Use Replay ID as an opaque pointer into the retained stream—never compute the next ID.
State that events are retained on the bus for 72 hours (three days) as documented, then missed events need another recovery path.
diagnostic_question: A subscriber was down for four hours. How do you resume with a stored Replay ID, what must you never compute, and when is 72-hour retention not enough?
definition: Platform events and Change Data Capture (CDC) events are published to the Salesforce event bus, a time-ordered log. Pub/Sub API (gRPC, protocol buffers, Avro payloads) publishes, subscribes, and retrieves schema. Each delivered event includes an opaque Replay ID locating it in the stream so a subscriber can resume inside the retention window—documented as 72 hours / three days. Do not synthesize new Replay IDs. ([Event durability](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-message-durability.html); [Event bus](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/expanded-event-bus.html); [CDC delivery](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.change_data_capture.meta/change_data_capture/cdc_subscribe_delivery.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers fail people who treat events as guaranteed forever queues, who compute Replay IDs, or who use CDC when they needed a custom platform event (or the reverse).
sixty_second_explanation: Picture a radio station with a 72-hour DVR. Platform events are shows you scheduled. CDC is the automatic recording of record-change headlines. Pub/Sub API is the studio feed. The Replay ID is an opaque ticket stub printed on each clip—you can rewind to a stub you kept, but you must not invent the next stub number. After 72 hours the DVR overwrites; you need another recovery path.
deeper_explanation: The event bus stores platform events and CDC events in arrival order for 72 hours. Pub/Sub API is the modern external client interface (gRPC/HTTP2, Avro). Clients request event counts per Subscribe fetch. ([Event bus](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/expanded-event-bus.html))

Replay ID is opaque, populated on delivery, not guaranteed contiguous. Subscribers store it and resubscribe after that ID. Do not compute new IDs. Replay ID uniqueness can break across org-migration maintenance; use the event id field to identify a platform event message. ([Durability](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-message-durability.html))

CDC events represent committed record changes and share storage characteristics with platform events (three days). Order follows committed transactions. ([CDC delivery](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.change_data_capture.meta/change_data_capture/cdc_subscribe_delivery.htm))

Managed subscriptions (beta/managed subscribe) can store committed Replay IDs on the server—confirm current GA/beta status before an interview deep-dive. CometD/EMP is a neighboring subscribe path; prefer Pub/Sub for new external clients unless a documented constraint says otherwise. Custom platform event definitions are metadata; the messages are data.

mental_model.analogy: A radio DVR with opaque ticket stubs: 72-hour tape, scheduled shows (platform events), news headlines of record changes (CDC), studio gRPC feed (Pub/Sub), stubs you keep (Replay ID).
useful_mapping: CDC → automatic headline of a record change
Replay ID → opaque stub; do not mint the next number
event id → identity when stubs collide after maintenance
event definition → program listing (metadata); messages → broadcasts (data)
where_it_breaks: Not a durable enterprise queue with infinite retention.
CDC is not a full row replica API like Bulk query.
Replay does not replace nightly batch reconciliation (INT-003/INT-010).
Do not invent CometD field lists here.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Custom platform events are signals you define. CDC is the bus recording record changes. Pub/Sub is how external systems tap the 72-hour log. Replay ID is an opaque stub you store and resume from—never add one.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: If a subscriber is down four hours, replay from the last stub. If down five days, the tape is gone; I need batch reconciliation. CDC follows committed transactions. Event definitions are metadata; messages are data. I will not invent delivery SLAs.

terminology.plain: A message type you define for business signals.
terminology.precise: Event published to the event bus (often custom). Distinct from CDC, which is generated from record changes.
terminology.example: LAB_Shipment_Ready__e published when a lab shipment is packed.
terminology.non_example: AccountChangeEvent when you really wanted a custom packed signal with extra payload.
terminology.boundary: Publish-immediate vs after-commit options: verify current PE guide.

terminology.precise: Change events stored like platform events for three days; order follows committed transactions; ReplayId for replay.
terminology.example: Subscribe to LAB_Item__c changes to sync a cache.
terminology.non_example: Bulk query of all items as if it were CDC.
terminology.boundary: Which objects are enabled is org configuration.

terminology.plain: The modern feed to publish and subscribe on the bus.
terminology.precise: gRPC API with protocol buffers; Avro event payloads; subscribe/publish/schema; binary async stream per Trailhead.
terminology.example: External Java client Subscribe RPC for a CDC channel.
terminology.boundary: Proto file lives in Salesforce's pubsub repo; do not invent RPCs.

terminology.plain: Opaque ticket stub on each delivered clip.
terminology.precise: ConsumerEvent.replay_id / ReplayId identifying position; not contiguous; do not compute new values; store and resume after it.
terminology.example: Persist last processed Replay ID in the subscriber store.
terminology.boundary: Not unique across some maintenance; use event id.

terminology.precise: Multitenant time-ordered event log storing PE and CDC for 72 hours.
terminology.example: Retrieve missed events after a four-hour outage.
terminology.non_example: Infinite Kafka-like retention you assume without a contract.
terminology.boundary: Retention is documented as 72 hours/three days—reverify if asked for minutes.

terminology.plain: The identity of the message when stubs collide.
terminology.precise: Use event id (ProducerEvent.id / ConsumerEvent.event.id) to uniquely identify a platform event, especially across org migration when replay_id uniqueness is not guaranteed.
terminology.example: Deduplicate on event id after a maintenance window.
terminology.non_example: Using Replay ID as a primary key forever.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Salesforce record Id of the changed Account.
terminology.boundary: CDC payload still includes record identifiers separately.

terminology.plain: How a Subscribe call chooses where to start on the tape.
terminology.precise: Subscribe RPC option to receive events after a Replay ID (or other documented presets). Confirm enum names in the current proto/docs.
terminology.example: Resume after stored Replay ID following a restart.

terminology.plain: How long the DVR keeps clips.
terminology.precise: 72 hours / three days for PE and CDC as cited. After that, replay cannot recover; use batch (INT-003/010).
terminology.example: Outage of five days needs a backfill job.
terminology.non_example: Assuming seven-year archive on the bus.

when_to_use: When you need platform events, Change Data Capture, Pub/Sub API, and replay concepts for event-driven integration.
When an external system should subscribe with an opaque Replay ID inside the 72-hour window.
When record-change headlines (CDC) fit better than a custom platform event, or the reverse.
When a subscriber outage is measured in hours versus days (replay vs batch backfill).
When you must refuse computed Replay IDs in a code review.
when_not_to_use: Do not use the event bus as infinite storage or as Bulk query replacement.
Do not page events with nextRecordsUrl (INT-005) or invent Replay ID arithmetic.
Do not put secrets in event payloads.
Do not skip INT-008 retries/idempotency because 'events are reliable forever'.
Do not enable CDC on every object in production from this lesson.

interview_questions.question: Explain platform events, CDC, Pub/Sub API, and replay.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: PE is a defined signal. CDC is record-change events. Pub/Sub is the gRPC feed. Replay ID is an opaque 72-hour stub you store and resume from.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I never add one to Replay ID. After 72 hours I backfill. Event id identifies PE messages across maintenance. Definitions are metadata; messages are data.

interview_questions.question: Why must Replay IDs not be computed?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: They are opaque and not guaranteed contiguous. Computing last+1 can skip or invent positions.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The durability guide is explicit. I store the bytes/value I received. For identity I use event id when uniqueness of Replay ID is not guaranteed.

interview_questions.question: Warehouse wants packed notifications; analytics wants item field changes.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Packed: platform event. Item fields: CDC. Both can use Pub/Sub. Different channels, different payloads.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I will not overload CDC to carry a packed flag that is not a field change. I will not publish a platform event for every field edit if CDC already exists. Replay stores are per subscription.
interview_questions.example: Two LAB_ channels in one sandbox design.

interview_questions.question: Subscriber crashed Friday and returned Wednesday.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: That gap exceeds 72 hours. Replay cannot recover the weekend. Schedule a batch reconcile, then resume live subscribe.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I timestamp the last successful Replay ID but I do not pretend the bus kept five days. INT-010 owns reconciliation keys. I communicate data-loss risk honestly.
interview_questions.example: Cache of LAB_Item__c stale after a long outage.

interview_questions.question: Duplicates after an org migration weekend.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Replay IDs may not be unique across maintenance. Deduplicate with event id and idempotency keys (INT-008).
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not blame Pub/Sub first. Official durability notes say Replay IDs may not stay unique across some org changes, so I deduplicate with event id plus an idempotency key (INT-008). CDC still follows commit order for new deliveries going forward.
interview_questions.example: Two deliveries with different Replay IDs and same event id.

interview_questions.question: Client uses REST query to 'subscribe'.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Wrong API. Point them to Pub/Sub. Query locators are INT-005.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Polling SOQL can approximate badly and burns API limits (INT-005). CDC/PE on the bus is the event-driven style (INT-003).
interview_questions.example: ETL that ran SELECT every 30 seconds instead of CDC.

interview_questions.question: Where do you store Replay IDs?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: In the subscriber's durable store, opaque. Optionally ManagedSubscribe if current docs say it is available.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat the store as operational data, backed up, not in a public custom object without security. I will not invent Salesforce-side default tables unless documenting ManagedSubscribe.
interview_questions.example: Redis/SQL table of channel plus replay bytes.

interview_questions.question: Teach the radio-DVR analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: 72-hour tape, shows vs headlines, gRPC feed, opaque stubs. It breaks if I promise infinite tape or Replay arithmetic.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map platform events, CDC, Pub/Sub, and replay, then say a batch backfill is the recovery truck after the 72-hour tape is overwritten. Governors and API allocations are not station wattage I invent, and Replay IDs stay opaque.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard a four-hour outage versus a five-day outage on the same CDC channel.
